purpose: Record the reasoning used to revise an explanatory series; no semantic admission or implementation verdict.

title_analysis.basis: The inspected technical essays and primary publications use titles that name the subject or central contribution. Mensh and Kording explicitly connect a title with a paper's central argument. This supports a direct descriptive title; it is not an authorship-detection claim.
alternatives_considered: The governance and operating model of CyberAlchemy Lab
How CyberAlchemy Lab organizes agent work
title_analysis.selection_reason: Covers both parts without implying that every described mechanism is already operational. Each chapter names one concrete argument.

editorial_principles: Begin with an interpretable case, then introduce the concept needed to explain it.
Give each essay one argument and arrange paragraphs around its dependencies.
Reuse the export case to preserve continuity without forcing every concept into it.
Keep full identifiers, schemas and finite enumerations in an inspectable reference section.
Attach external sources to the limited claim they support.
Describe proposed business applications as illustrative cases, not measured deployments.
Distinguish normative source meaning from this explanatory synthesis.
Preserve exact source selections, recorded acceptance and the strongest conclusions justified by the evidence.

remaining_model_questions.subject: Governance lenses: authority, provenance and lifecycle
remaining_model_questions.finding: The proposed module describes authority mainly as decision rights. Accepted definitions also govern meanings, record requirements and permitted connections.
remaining_model_questions.treatment: The essays explain the broader accepted model. Revising the proposed module requires its own review.

remaining_model_questions.subject: Keeping software aligned with accepted changes
remaining_model_questions.status: Update proposed; repeatable operation remains planned
remaining_model_questions.finding: The accepted local software uses an earlier selection of accepted records. A proposed successor selects the later Project State—the project’s saved records and knowledge—and has a captured report of passing checks. The successor still needs separate acceptance.
remaining_model_questions.treatment: The essays distinguish which source records the software selects, which implementation is accepted and what has been exercised.

remaining_model_questions.subject: Historical references that do not resolve
remaining_model_questions.finding: The software documentation reports older references that cannot be matched to the selected versions. Replacing their names would not resolve those missing bindings.
remaining_model_questions.treatment: The explanations keep these missing references and their limits visible when describing graph queries.

remaining_model_questions.subject: How much of the definition model has been formally proved?
remaining_model_questions.status: Partial translation; no complete definition proofs
remaining_model_questions.finding: The captured coverage report lists 183 current definition identities. Three have source-linked partial pilot translations, and eight have source-linked notes on the formal foundation. It reports zero verified proofs covering whole definitions.
remaining_model_questions.treatment: The essays explain non-collapse—finding cases that distinguish meanings—as one assurance method. They make no claim of proven global consistency or complete proof coverage.

remaining_model_questions.subject: Which sources does the ontology cover?
remaining_model_questions.status: Coverage is limited to declared source sets
remaining_model_questions.finding: The ontology import contains 21 packages, and the local software selects particular source records. Their manifests identify bounded source sets. These records do not establish coverage of every current repository object or the existence of a continuously running service.
remaining_model_questions.treatment: Read a graph result relative to its declared sources and the question it was constructed to answer.

remaining_model_questions.subject: Has a particular implementation been adopted for a capability?
remaining_model_questions.finding: References from the accepted implementation to a capability do not establish a separately adopted Capability Realization Binding—the record selecting how that capability will be delivered—or a declared realizes connection.
remaining_model_questions.treatment: The essays distinguish an association, acceptance of implementation, adoption for a capability, activation and observed benefit.

remaining_model_questions.subject: What does Projection Specification mean in its source?
remaining_model_questions.status: Possible mismatch between the name and intended meaning
remaining_model_questions.finding: The selected definition’s governing wording concerns a concept that requires a governed information view. Its name alone does not establish a formal contract for mapping source data into a projection.
remaining_model_questions.treatment: The library retains the exact governing statement and does not invent additional requirements from the term’s name.

remaining_model_questions.subject: Is there a stable release?
remaining_model_questions.finding: The accepted local foundation is distinct from the proposed work needed for repeatable operation, integration, ontology coverage and a usable product. Stable-release prerequisites remain separate.
remaining_model_questions.treatment: The essays explain the accepted foundation and the remaining stages without presenting a plan as an achieved outcome.
